summary: Initial scoping for a 4-week pilot to validate latency and cost under mixed steady and bursty traffic. Plan includes replaying anonymized logs, synthetic stress tests, three model-variant comparisons, and a 48-hour soak. Acceptance gates: p95 latency targets, soak stability, burst resiliency, and cost projection within 15% of quote.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-08T16:00:00-07:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (ZenCommerce SRE), Maya Li (Platform PM), Omar Khan (Eng Lead)

[00:00:03] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick agenda - scope the POC, walk through workload characterization, nail down success criteria and timelines. Priya and I will drive tech/Qs.
[00:00:18] Jordan: Great, thanks Alex. We're mostly focused on low-latency chat completions and some background summarization jobs. We want to validate cost too, obviously.
[00:00:30] Priya (SE): Perfect. Jordan, can you remind us of current traffic shape - QPS, concurrency, token lengths?
[00:00:38] Jordan: Sure. Right now prod chat front-end averages ~3 QPS per region (~9 global), but spikes during campaigns to ~20-75 QPS short bursts. Concurrency ~40 active sessions at peaks. Avg user turns ~60 input tokens / ~120 output tokens. Long-run flows (invoicing, summaries) push outputs to 2k-2.5k tokens occasionally.
[00:01:07] Maya: Majority of requests under 200 tokens, long tail small but business-critical.
[00:01:15] Alex: So baseline is sustained low QPS with bursty spikes. Priya - how simulate long tail?
[00:01:27] Priya: Mixed traffic model: 70% small chat (60/120 tokens), 25% mid (200-600 tokens), 5% long-form (1k-2.5k). Replay anonymized logs and synthetic Poisson bursts to hit peaks. Replay gives sequence length distribution for realistic batching and KV cache hit rates.
[00:01:58] Omar: For long docs we stream tokens, so first-byte vs tail latency matters.
[00:02:10] Priya: For interactive we recommend p95 < 500ms for short turns and p95 < 2s for mid-size depending on model size. Long-form is about throughput and cost.
[00:02:25] Jordan: Internal goal p95 < 600ms for 200 token responses and p99 < 2s. Realistic with dedicated capacity?
[00:02:33] Priya: Yes with dedicated GPU pools and tuned batching. Big 2k responses at sub-second p95 improbable without high-end GPUs and aggressive quantization.
[00:02:48] Alex: Cost tradeoffs - Jordan, target cost-per-1k-output?
[00:02:55] Jordan: We'd like <$0.50 per 1k output tokens as a runway number.
[00:03:03] Priya: We'll model three variants: small quantized (8-bit), medium (16-bit), larger for long-tail. Bench will show cost/latency curves.
[00:03:19] Maya: Timeline? Need results before exec review on 2025-05-22.
[00:03:25] Alex: Proposed 4-week pilot: Week 0 agree scope/exchange logs/sign quote. Week 1 infra setup + small synthetic runs. Week 2 replay logs + spike tests + 48-hour soak. Week 3 tuning + E2E integration. Week 4 finalize metrics and exec report.
[00:03:50] Jordan: If logs by 2025-05-14 you can start Week 1?
[00:03:55] Priya: Yes. Need S3 or secure transfer plus tokenizer config.
[00:04:05] Omar: How model KV cache benefits? Frontend reuses recent context.
[00:04:13] Priya: Harness will simulate cache-hit by replaying session continuity. We'll run cases with/without prefix caching. Expect cost reductions if reuse >30-40%. Include cold-start case.
[00:04:30] Alex: Also capture routing/fallback: failover to hosted lower-cost models?
[00:04:38] Priya: Yes, test smart routing policies: prefer dedicated low-latency pods, fallback to hosted variant, track user-visible latency and model deltas.
[00:04:51] Jordan: Compliance - need audit log retention and encryption details for SOC2.
[00:04:58] Alex: We'll share security pack link after call.
[00:05:07] Maya: Proposed success criteria: p95 short chat <600ms; sustained 20 QPS for 24h with <2% error; handle 75 QPS bursts for 10 min with graceful degradation; cost projection within 15% of pilot quote.
[00:05:32] Priya: We'll add 48-hour soak <0.5% dropped requests and regression check on your 50-prompt eval.
[00:05:45] Omar: Need hallucination metrics for invoice summarization.
[00:05:50] Priya: We'll surface ROUGE/accuracy metrics and run custom validators during replay.
[00:06:05] Jordan: Can you replay at 2x for headroom?
[00:06:10] Priya: Yes: nominal, 2x, and burst tests. Also Poisson synthetic to estimate tail.
[00:06:21] Alex: Measurement points: per-request model variant, input/output tokens, queue time, compute time, KV hit/miss, p50/p95/p99 latency, error code, cost estimate. Dashboards provided.
[00:06:36] Maya: Dashboard retention - 30 days raw traces during POC?
[00:06:40] Priya: Yes, pilot includes 30-day retention and CSV export.
[00:06:47] Jordan: Gotchas - custom tokenizer for legal snippets. Will include tokenizer config.
[00:06:56] Priya: Tokenization differences can change batching and KV behavior; critical to share.
[00:07:04] Omar: Infra - VPC peering or public endpoint with IP allowlist?
[00:07:10] Alex: Pilot can use public IP allowlist with encrypted ingress; VPC peering adds ~1 week to provisioning.
[00:07:20] Maya: Public with IP allowlist is fine for pilot.
[00:07:27] Priya: Bench will measure batching efficiency: avg batch size vs seq length. Short sequences pack well; long sequences reduce batching and increase latency.
[00:07:41] Jordan: Recommend autobalance policies? We prefer latency over cost.
[00:07:47] Priya: Will set latency-first routing for pilot and provide cost/latency toggle.
[00:07:56] Alex: Bench matrix?
[00:08:01] Priya: Matrix: three model variants (small-quantized, medium-16-bit, large-16/32-bit), three traffic modes (steady 20 QPS, burst 75 QPS for 10 min, replay 7-day sample at 1x/2x), two cache configs (KV enabled, KV disabled). For each run capture metrics and run 48-hour soak on steady 20 QPS.
[00:08:26] Maya: Whitelist test accounts/feature flags?
[00:08:30] Alex: Need test API keys and staging front-end. Jordan/Omar to provision staging tenant and credentials.
[00:08:40] Omar: Do you support per-request KV eviction TTLs?
[00:08:47] Priya: Yes, TTL-based eviction and per-tenant max prefix size. Will set conservative defaults.
[00:08:55] Jordan: How handle function/tool calls and structured outputs in tests?
[00:09:00] Priya: Replay function call traces and validate structured outputs. Emulate external tool calls to avoid hitting prod 3rd-party APIs. Instrument end-to-end latency impact.
[00:09:12] Alex: Any measurement accuracy questions?
[00:09:16] Maya: Replay logs have user ids; we'll anonymize but keep session continuity.
[00:09:23] Priya: Session continuity matters for KV cache.
[00:09:27] Jordan: How handle failures during spikes - queue or reject?
[00:09:31] Priya: Configurable. Default to bounded queue + fast-fail fallback to hosted model variant. Also include soft degradation (reduce model size) strategy.
[00:09:45] Omar: Monitoring and alerts - can you tie into PagerDuty?
[00:09:49] Alex: Provide webhook alerts and can send to staging PD rota. Thresholds set by SLOs.
[00:09:56] Maya: Legal - need a DPA for logs during pilot.
[00:10:02] Alex: Will attach DPA template.
[00:10:06] Priya: We'll produce effective tokens-per-second and cost-per-effective-token metrics accounting for KV reuse and batching. Also track quantization regressions (BLEU/ROUGE deltas) if requested.
[00:10:33] Alex: Pilot acceptance criteria recap?
[00:10:40] Maya: 1) p95 short chat <600ms, 2) 48-hour soak at 20 QPS with <0.5% errors, 3) burst resiliency to 75 QPS for 10 min with graceful fallback, 4) cost projection within 15% of quote and quality parity on 50-prompt eval.
[00:10:59] Alex: We'll include scorecard in final report.
[00:11:06] Priya: Also provide token-level billing simulation for finance.
[00:11:23] Jordan: We'll want quantization impact included.
[00:11:25] Maya: Timeline with logs by 2025-05-14: baseline report by 2025-05-20, soak completed by 2025-05-26, final report by 2025-05-30, exec review 2025-06-03.
[00:11:42] Omar: Tight but doable.
[00:11:44] Jordan: Do you require disabling our rate-limiter during replays?
[00:11:50] Priya: Prefer no external rate-limiting for replay. Coordinate permissive staging limits.
[00:12:00] Alex: Recap next steps: Alex sends pilot quote + DPA + security pack; Priya sends bench harness + config; Jordan uploads logs + staging creds; schedule deep-dive on 2025-05-15.
[00:12:18] Maya: Confirmed.
[00:12:20] Jordan: Starting log export today.
[00:12:24] Omar: Adding custom tokenizer config.
[00:12:28] Alex: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up this week.
[00:12:33] (end of recorded portion)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache), filler words and overlaps.

References mentioned: https://redwood.ai/docs/pilot-playbook , https://redwood.ai/security/pilot-scc , internal bench harness repo.

Observed workload quick stats from call: Sustained QPS per region: ~3 QPS; Global baseline QPS: ~9 QPS; Campaign spike QPS: 20-75 QPS; Peak concurrency: ~40 sessions; Avg input tokens: ~60; Avg output tokens: ~120; Long-tail outputs: 1k-2.5k tokens (~5% traffic).

Bench acceptance metrics: p95/p99 latencies, error rate, KV hit rate, cost per 1k output tokens, quality regression on 50-prompt eval.

End of file.
